title: UL-07 — Challenge: EC2, EBS, and EFS
scenario: Add a small Amazon EFS file system to the EC2/EBS pattern: mount, write, unmount, delete.
acceptanceCriteria: Name the resources you create `workbook-ul07`: file system tagged Name=workbook-ul07, EC2 instance tagged Name=workbook-ul07, mount-target security group `workbook-ul07-mt-sg`, and instance security group `workbook-ul07-sg`. Tag each one LabId=ul-07.
A small EFS file system is created with encryption at rest enabled.
One mount target exists in the same VPC/AZ as a lab EC2 instance.
You mount the file system on the instance and create one test file.
You read the file back successfully.
You unmount before terminating the instance.
EC2 instance is terminated, not merely stopped.
EFS mount targets are deleted before file system delete.
File system delete completes without MountTargetConflict.
Security groups allow NFS only from the instance SG.
describe-file-systems shows none for your id.

hints.text: EFS mount targets bill per AZ.

solution.outline: EFS integrated EC2 lab with teardown.

stopChargesPanel: Unmount EFS on the instance, delete the mount targets and wait until none remain, delete the EFS file system, terminate the EC2 instance, then delete the mount-target SG and the instance SG for ul-07. Forgotten 24 h ≈ $0.72 (cautious, not calculated; see the cost basis).

orderedDeletesPowerShell: # Uses: $FileSystemId, $InstanceId, $MountTargetSgId, $InstanceSgId (the IDs you set while building; unset ones are skipped)
# Lost an ID? Resources are named workbook-ul07*; list what is tagged with aws resourcegroupstaggingapi get-resources --tag-filters Key=LabId,Values=ul-07
# First unmount on the instance: sudo umount <mountpoint>

if ($FileSystemId) { $MtIds = aws efs describe-mount-targets --file-system-id $FileSystemId --query "MountTargets[].[MountTargetId]" --output text; foreach ($MtId in $MtIds) { if ($MtId) { aws efs delete-mount-target --mount-target-id $MtId } } }

if ($FileSystemId) { $i = 0; do { Start-Sleep -Seconds 10; $MtLeft = aws efs describe-mount-targets --file-system-id $FileSystemId --query "length(MountTargets)" --output text; $i++ } while ($MtLeft -and $MtLeft -ne '0' -and $i -lt 60); if ($i -ge 60) { Write-Host 'Timed out waiting for EFS mount targets to delete after 60 tries; check the EFS console before deleting the file system' } }
if ($InstanceId) { aws ec2 terminate-instances --instance-ids $InstanceId; aws ec2 wait instance-terminated --instance-ids $InstanceId }
verification: aws resourcegroupstaggingapi get-resources --tag-filters Key=LabId,Values=ul-07 returns an empty ResourceTagMappingList in $env:AWS_REGION
aws efs describe-file-systems --file-system-id $FileSystemId returns FileSystemNotFound (it can take a minute after delete-file-system)
aws ec2 describe-instances --instance-ids $InstanceId shows State.Name terminated
teardown.stillBillingNote: Time already used, transfer, tax, and 8–12h billing lag may still appear. Alerts do not delete resources.
teardown.recovery: If teardown fails, stop. Confirm $env:AWS_REGION is us-east-1 and the caller is not root. Run aws sts get-caller-identity and type that Account value before any delete. List LabId=ul-07 with aws resourcegroupstaggingapi get-resources --tag-filters Key=LabId,Values=ul-07. Delete only those ids. Never delete untagged resources. If delete-file-system returns FileSystemInUse, wait a minute and rerun the mount-target poll line.

beforeYouStart: Read the paired guided lab (gl-07) stop-charges panel before you create anything.
Set $env:AWS_PROFILE and $env:AWS_REGION. Do not use the root user.

Cost basis (us-east-1, priced 2026-09-29): t3.micro $0.0104/h (smallest assumed), 1 public IPv4 $0.005/h, 8 GB gp3 root, plus EFS storage. The EFS rate was not read on 2026-09-29, so check the EFS pricing page before you run. This run ≈ $0.04 (EFS not included); forgotten 24 h ≈ $0.72, a cautious figure, not a calculated one (the parts we could price come to about $0.39). Not included: data transfer.
